title: chore(claude): allow the edit tools on the os-dev worktrees' .changeset/pre notes
body:
Fixes #23860
Clause-②: no

## What this does

One row is added to `permissions.allow` in `.claude/settings.json`, and nothing else in the file changes:

```text
"Edit(//home/user/objectstack-issue-*/.changeset/pre/**)",
```

It sits after `mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger` and before `Bash(agent-browser snapshot *)`. This places the new built-in-tool family between the `mcp__` rows and the `Bash(...)` rows, so no neighbouring line changes. Counts: `allow` 78 → 79, `deny` 17 unchanged, no `ask` key. The diff is +1 line.

Why: an auto-mode dev session edits in a sibling worktree, outside its primary working directory. Its edit of a consumed `.changeset/pre/` note therefore falls to the auto-mode classifier, which refused the maintainer-confirmed correction on #23447 as "Modify Shared Resources". An allow rule resolves before the classifier.

## How this edit was made

The first dev round could not make it. This session's auto-mode classifier refused the `Edit` of `.claude/settings.json` as `[Self-Modification]`: `.claude` is a protected path, and no allow rule pre-approves writes there. The round reported `blocked` with the row and the anchor choice as open questions (report comment 6214588473). The maintainer then turned auto mode off in this session, in their words: 「我去掉auto了，你再试试」. The edit was made through the permission prompt that followed. The anchor is option A, the dev's recommendation, which the seat chose on that word.

## The three premises (card Acceptance), with the documentation

Placeholders the docs write in angle brackets are spelled here in square brackets, for the GitHub body sanitizer.

### 1. The rule's path spelling

**1a. The anchor.** `//path` anchors at the filesystem root. `/path` anchors at the primary working directory for project settings. A bare `path` anchors at the current directory. In a dispatched dev session both of the last two are the shared checkout (`/home/user/objectstack`, measured with `pwd`), and a `cd` into the sibling worktree does not move them. So only a `//` row can name `/home/user/objectstack-issue-N/`.

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Read and Edit): "| `//path` | Absolute path from filesystem root | `Read(//Users/alice/secrets/**)` | `/Users/alice/secrets/**` |"
- same: "| `/path` | Path relative to the settings source | `Edit(/src/**/*.ts)` | `[primary working directory]/src/**/*.ts` in project settings |"
- same: "| `path` or `./path` | Path relative to current directory | `Read(*.env)` | `[cwd]/*.env` |"
- same: "A pattern like `/Users/alice/file` isn't an absolute path. The single leading slash anchors at the settings source, not the filesystem root. Use `//Users/alice/file` for absolute paths."
- same: "| Project settings at `.claude/settings.json` | `[primary working directory]/path` |"
- same: "A rule only matches files under its anchor"
- same: "`Edit(//tmp/scratch.txt)`: edits the absolute path `/tmp/scratch.txt`"
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference (Bash): "If `cd` lands outside those directories, Claude Code resets to the project directory and appends `Shell cwd was reset to [dir]` to the tool result." and "Subagent sessions never carry over working directory changes."

**1b. One `Edit(...)` row covers `Write`.** It also covers every other built-in editing tool. The card's second row, `Write(.changeset/pre/**)`, would never be consulted and would raise a startup warning, so it is not added.

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Read and Edit): "`Edit` rules apply to all built-in tools that edit files."
- same: "Claude Code checks file permissions against `Edit(path)` and `Read(path)` rules only. If you write a path rule for `Write`, `NotebookEdit`, `Glob`, or the legacy `MultiEdit` tool instead, Claude Code accepts the rule but never consults it, and warns at startup, except for a `Glob` rule passed in `--allowedTools`. Use `Edit(docs/**)` in place of `Write(docs/**)`, `NotebookEdit(docs/**)`, or `MultiEdit(docs/**)`"

### 2. An allow rule decides before the auto-mode classifier, for file-edit rules too

Holds. The decision order is the same for every tool, and `.changeset` is not in the protected-directory list. The same text explains the original refusal. Step 2 auto-approves only edits inside the working directory, so a worktree edit fell to step 3.

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (How the classifier evaluates actions): "Each action goes through a fixed decision order. The first matching step wins: 1. Actions matching your allow, ask, or deny rules resolve immediately, with these exceptions: Writes to protected paths route to the classifier even when an allow rule matches"
- same: "2. Read-only actions and file edits in your working directory are auto-approved, except writes to protected paths" … "3. Everything else goes to the classifier"
- The classifier-side alternative is not available from this file. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config: "The classifier doesn't read `autoMode` from project settings in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`."

### 3. Which sessions the rule reaches

Partly falsified. A session reads the settings file in its own project directory, which is the shared checkout, never a worktree copy. That file is watched and reloaded, permissions included. So the row reaches a session from the moment the shared checkout's file on disk carries it, a running session included: at clone for a new cloud session, or when the shared checkout moves to a `main` that has it. Project allow rows also need workspace trust. The rows PR #19047 added show they apply in cloud sessions; this was not re-measured here.

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings (When edits take effect): "Claude Code watches your settings files and reloads them when they change, so it applies most edits to the running session without a restart, including edits to `permissions`, `hooks`, and credential helpers such as `apiKeyHelper`."
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions: "Hooks and other `.claude/settings.json` keys load from the current working directory's `.claude/` folder with no parent-directory fallback"
- same (Project allow rules and workspace trust): "`permissions.allow` rules and `permissions.additionalDirectories` entries in a project's `.claude/settings.json` grant capability, so Claude Code applies them only after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder."

## What the row matches, and what it does not

Simulated with gitignore syntax (`ignore@5.3.2`), with each anchor placed as the docs state. This is a reading of the pattern, not of Claude Code's own matcher.

| path | this row | `/.changeset/pre/**` (the card's literal reading) | `//**/.changeset/pre/**` |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `/home/user/objectstack-issue-23447/.changeset/pre/23357-…md` | match | no | match |
| `/home/user/objectstack-issue-23447-cmp/.changeset/pre/x.md` | match | no | match |
| `/home/user/objectstack/.changeset/pre/…md` (shared checkout) | no | match | match |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/.changeset/pre.json` | no | no | no |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/.changeset/*.md` (pending notes) | no | no | no |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/.changeset/config.json` | no | no | no |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` | no | no | no |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/content/docs/releases/…` | no | no | no |
| `…/objectstack-issue-N/.claude/settings.json` | no | no | no |
| `/home/user/objectui/.changeset/pre/x.md`, `/home/user/objectui-issue-1/…` | no | no | match |
| `/home/user/objectstack-23447/.changeset/pre/x.md` (no `issue`) | no | no | match |
| `/tmp/objectstack-issue-1/…`, `/root/objectstack-issue-1/…` | no | no | match |
| `…/objectstack-issue-1/node_modules/pkg/.changeset/pre/x.md` | no | no | match |

The card's literal reading matches only the shared checkout. Dev sessions never edit there: the guard hook blocks it, and step 2 already auto-approves it. So for the refused workflow it would be a no-op. `//**/.changeset/pre/**` breaches the card's "Nothing wider" list. This row is inert wherever the checkout does not sit under `/home/user`, a local machine for example; that leaves a gap and does no harm.

**Side effect, stated rather than added.** Output-redirect and `tee` targets are checked against `Edit` allow rules. So this row also clears the target check for a Bash redirect or `tee` into these files, while the Bash command itself is judged as before. No `Bash(...)` row is added.

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Redirections): "for `> file`, `>> file`, or `2> file`, the check covers your `Edit` allow and deny rules, protected paths, and the working directories." and "Claude Code also checks the files a `tee` command writes … The check covers your `Edit` allow and deny rules"

## What still guards a consumed note

- The DELIBERATE CORRECTION route. It lives in `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`: the foreign-changeset rule header, and `FOREIGN_CORRECTION_REMEDY` ("do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed"). It also lives in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md`, where the confirmation must name every edited note. It is not in `AGENTS.md` (0 occurrences).
- `Check Changeset`. Its pathspec `.changeset/*.md` covers all 714 `.changeset/pre/` notes (a git pathspec `*` crosses `/`; `git ls-files -- '.changeset/*.md'` gives 714 under `pre/`), so an edited consumed note reds it.
- The seat's review of record.

No `deny` row interacts with this one. All 17 are `mcp__github__` tools, and no user, local or managed settings exist in the measuring container.

## Verification at `17f7ad57e`

- `node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(".claude/settings.json","utf8"))'` exited 0.
- `node scripts/pm/check-settings-deny-roster.mjs` exited 0: "✓ check-settings-deny-roster: 17 content-write tool(s) declared = enforced in .claude/settings.json (17 mcp__github__ deny entr(ies), 0 outside this gate's population and ignored)."
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` was re-derived with no paths after the final commit. Change set: 1 path vs merge base `2034975a4`, giving 16 commands. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all 16 exited 0. On its first run, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: no `formula`/`lint` dist in the fresh worktree). It exited 0 after the build it prescribes, which ran under the verify lock.
- `--ran`: "✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 16 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 16 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 16 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)."
- No changeset: `.claude/**` publishes nothing.
- The live pin in the card's Acceptance comes after landing: the next maintainer-confirmed `.changeset/pre/` correction made by an auto-mode dev session without a refusal. It is the seat's to record.

## Acceptance notes

- Observation, not filed. Any later `.claude/settings.json` change authored by an auto-mode session meets the same `[Self-Modification]` refusal, by design: the docs route protected-path writes to the classifier whatever the allow rules say. This edit needed the maintainer's own action in the session.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么**:`.claude/settings.json` 的 `permissions.allow` 里只加了一行 `Edit(//home/user/objectstack-issue-*/.changeset/pre/**)`,文件其余部分不变。

**为什么改**:云端开发会话是在仓库旁边的 worktree 里改文件的,这些编辑不在会话的工作目录内,所以交给 auto 模式分类器判断。维护者已经确认的「已消费 changeset 更正」(`.changeset/pre/` 下的文件)因此被分类器以「修改共享资源」拒掉,只能由席位代改。允许规则在分类器之前生效,加上这一行,这类更正就不会再被拦。路径必须写成文件系统绝对路径:按项目根写的规则只会落到共享检出上,碰不到 worktree。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**:只放行 `/home/user/objectstack-issue-*/` 这些 worktree 下 `.changeset/pre/` 里的文件。pending changeset、`pre.json`、各包 `CHANGELOG.md`、`content/docs/releases/`、共享检出和 objectui 都不在内。副作用:Bash 用重定向或 `tee` 写这些文件时,目标检查也一并放行(命令本身仍照原样判)。仍在把关的有三道:`Check Changeset` 对改动过的已消费 note 会变红;DELIBERATE CORRECTION 流程要求维护者在 PR 上书面确认;席位复核。代价:路径写死了云容器的 `/home/user` 布局,在本地机器上这一行不生效,但也无害。回滚:revert 本 PR 删掉这一行即可;设置文件是热加载的,改动立即生效。

**席位意见**:

**你要做的**:无需操作。这是 Tier S 改动,由席位做达档复核后落地。落地后,下一次经维护者确认的 `.changeset/pre/` 更正如果在 auto 模式的开发会话里顺利完成、没有被拒,席位会在 #23860 上记录,作为验收。
